cultural.vision_reason: A beaded bustle medallion with feather back-ornament used in Plains-style dance regalia; such beadwork and bustle ornaments are made and worn across Pueblo peoples including the Tewa, so this fits the claimed culture's material culture.

physical.title: regalia; back-ornament (upper); medallion
physical.summary: Upper back bustle and bustle medallion.  The bustle is constructed of sticks wrapped in tape and coloured string, with feathers and orange strips of synthetic material streaming at the ends.  The sticks are threaded together with cord.  A wooden block is used to attach the bustle to the body, with holes to receive the cord (shoelace) which will be used to tie the bustle to the body.  The wooden block also gets concealed by a bustle medallion, which is constructed of two layers of cardboard discs, which are decorated and layered, the smaller on the larger; and attached with shoelaces threaded through the two disc layers.  The smallest top layer disc is constructed beaded hide with a rhinestone in the centre; the beads are white, blue, yellow, orange and red.  The larger disc is constructed of a three-layer cardboard backing with maroon feathers mounted on the front. Part of an ensemble of powwow regalia.
